{"decision": "propose", "selected": ["gd01-late-boost-110", "gd01-mid-late-boost"], "reason": "Current best remains the constant-90 full-population measurement (ev identities calibration/frozen/478775c7fecfe6a2d08f41044ec851b516fe3b857f2593a05e9148c5a572cf67/population_50/69f59c273b6e669ac32a6dd5e1b2cb63333d8b004f9696447aee2d422ce63763), raw arithmetic mean conditional coordinate root mean square deviation 0.2792394658178091 A, 49 built / 49 connected of 50, maximum condition atom coordinate error 1.3528382778167725 A. The confirmed constant ladder falls off on both sides (80: 0.38432059325277806; 100: 0.33535465426743033; 110: 0.3738719318807125), and the three completed non-constant schedules are all mildly to moderately worse than the incumbent ([90,100,110,110,90] 0.2887168160825968 via versions/GD01/3w54_RNB_A_504/iteration_001/action_001, [90,90,80,80,90] 0.28503116622567176 via versions/GD01/3w54_RNB_A_504/iteration_002/action_001, [90,80,80,80,80] 0.30979996114969255 via versions/GD01/3w54_RNB_A_504/iteration_002/action_002). So the useful question is not another uniform level but which windows tolerate added strength.

I select the two proposals that keep the displacement phase at the measured best and spend the extra strength only in the second half, at two jump distances.

(1) gd01-late-boost-110 = [90,90,90,90,110], focused (+2 ticks, single-window change). In the small-population window diagnostics the 51-99 window stays cheap at every measured level (max atom increment about 0.08 A at 90, 0.24 A at 90 in the 20-attempt record, 0.42 A at 100, 0.55 A at 110, 0.19 A at 120) and its increment vector RMS is roughly an order of magnitude below window 0. This is the smallest legal perturbation of the incumbent on the axis where extra guidance cannot create large atom moves, so any loss should be small and the information about the terminal segment is clean.

(2) gd01-mid-late-boost = [90,100,100,100,110], expanded (+5 ticks, four windows). The measured mid-heavy probe gained only 0.010 A over the incumbent while adding strength in windows 1-3, and this variant asks for a smaller mid increment (+1 in windows 1-3 instead of +1/+2/+2) combined with the cheap terminal increase, i.e. a monotone rise through the refinement half with window 0 untouched. This is the broader joint adjustment worth testing given that both single-direction mid probes stayed within ~0.01 A of the best.

I decline gd01-trim-first-raise-rest ([80,110,110,110,110], bold, +9 ticks). Window 0 is the only segment where measured guidance produces extreme single-atom increments (14.65 A at constant 90, 23.88 A at constant 80), and lowering it contradicts both the best measurement and both near-incumbent probes, which all hold window 0 at 90; constant 80 as a whole schedule (0.3843) is the second-worst ranking-eligible configuration. Its upward half also relies on small populations (10 and 20 attempts) that are not rankable. That path is the most likely of the three to be clearly worse.

Unknowns: no completed schedule holds windows 0-3 at the incumbent and changes only window 4, and no completed schedule combines a mid increase with a terminal increase, so both selections are unmeasured directions; the terminal window contributes a small share of total displacement, so its gain could fall within 50-sample population noise; and because upward sensitivity is real (constant 100 costs 0.056 A), the four-window variant could accumulate small per-window losses into a clearly worse mean. These are exploration opportunities, not established mechanisms, and neither is claimed to beat 0.2792394658178091."}
